parsed.explanation: The visitor-facing picture is largely protective: no trans-specific entry or screening friction is documented, foreign documents with X markers are accepted, transphobia is criminally punishable, courts enforce anti-discrimination awards against venues that refuse trans patrons, official guidance affirms identity-based bathroom use, and a national custody resolution requires individualised, preference-based placement. Against this, the record documents significant LGBTQ-targeted violence and predatory robberies (drink-spiking, fatal dating-app lures) with no trans-disaggregated denominator, and documented divergence between the custody resolution and practice (trans women housed in masculine units in one state system) — a real exposure for any detained visitor, though the remedy mechanism exists. Most severe material (youth care bans, prison conditions, street sex work) is resident-facing; it colours but does not drive the score. This sits between the 0.65 anchors (dead-letter statutes, uneven remedies, predation risk) and 0.75 (working protections): roughly 0.65-0.70, set at 0.68.
